text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: ALB healthcheck failures increasing in eu-west-1a/euc1a and eu-west-1b; targetgroup api-backend returning TCP RSTs and 5xx surge. P90 latency spiking. Page: @Erin (primary)
Erin (on-call): Acked. I’m looking now. First callout: is this confined to eu region or cross-region? :eyes:
Jon (netops): Seeing unusual drops on NLB->targets in euc1a. TCP RST count up ~8x in the last 3m. ALB shows 502/504 mix. Route53 review: no recent changes. No deployments reported by deploy-bot yet.
Erin (on-call): @deploy-bot were there any recent rollout jobs? I need a cause check.
deploy-bot: No active deploys in the last 2 hours. Nightly canary passed earlier.
Anna (infra): Pulling EC2 metrics for euc1a. Network interface error counters rising on a subset of hosts (eni-0ab...). Also seeing sporadic kernel conntrack evictions on those instances.
Maya (eng-sre): If conntrack is evicting, Envoy will drop connections causing RSTs upstream. Can we confirm Envoy stats? Which rollout of sidecar? Also are ALB healthchecks failing or target marked unhealthy?
Jon (netops): ALB shows 12/50 targets unhealthy across euc1a and 2/40 in euc1b. Healthcheck failures are connection resets during /healthz probe. Envoy stats: active_connections spiked, downstream_cx_total rising, downstream_cx_destroy with error 'connection termination' on the same hosts.
Erin (on-call): Impact estimate? Luis can you summarize customer signals.
Luis (support): Support queue: 14 new tickets referencing 502/connection reset for generate endpoint in EU. Telemetry shows ~38% of requests to /v1/generate in EU failing. Some high-traffic customers seeing retries succeed (due to route fallback) but latency doubled.
Maya (eng-sre): Short-term mitigations: 1) Mark problematic targets out of ALB target group to stop serving. 2) Scale up healthy targets in other AZs (euc1c) and increase ALB weight shunt. 3) Bump conntrack on Linux hosts to reduce evictions. 4) Consider restarting Envoy on affected nodes after draining.
Erin (on-call): Doing 1 and 2 now. Jon, can you adjust target weights/failover? Anna, prepare conntrack sysctl changes and list of instance IDs to reboot if needed.
Jon (netops): I’m shifting 30% of ALB traffic away from euc1a to euc1c via target group weighting and temporary stickiness reset. Command I used:

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=slow_start.duration_seconds,Value=30
# then adjust weights in the routing table
```

Traffic awayshifting in progress. Observed drop in 5xx rate in next 60s.
Anna (infra): conntrack max set from 262144 -> 524288 on affected nodes (applied via SSM runbook). Reboot avoided for now. Monitoring kernel evictions.
Maya (eng-sre): Rolling restart of Envoy on the 8 worst hosts using drain+restart pattern. Code snippet:

```
kubectl -n infra exec -it envoy-pod-xx -- /bin/bash -c "curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:15000/quitquitquit"
kubectl rollout restart daemonset envoy -n infra --selector=host=affected
```

Started first two; healthchecks improving on those targets.
Erin (on-call): Good. Customer impact update: currently ~15% of EU traffic still seeing elevated errors, down from 38%. Global traffic unaffected. Logged affected customers list to incident tracker.
Luis (support): Notifying top 10 customers that reported errors. Draft message ready:

"We experienced elevated API errors in EU region; mitigation in progress. Some requests may have retried successfully; we're continuing to monitor. ETA for full recovery: 30-60m."

Approve? :thumbsup:
Erin (on-call): Send it. Also mention the mitigation steps and that engineering is investigating root cause.
Jon (netops): Additional note: We found an upstream network path issue between the AZ fabric and the i/o layer for a subset of hosts—packet drops causing conntrack entries to pile up. Eng infra is engaging cloud provider support.
Anna (infra): Provider support ticket opened: INC-112233. They've acknowledged and are looking at NIC firmware and hypervisor host health. ETA initial response 20m.
Maya (eng-sre): Next actions for RCA: collect /proc/net/nf_conntrack, envoy stats dump, kernel logs (dmesg) for affected hosts, ALB access logs. Will archive to incident S3.
Erin (on-call): Handoff plan: I'll own the next 30m, then hand to @Maya for deep-dive. On-call rotation: next on-call is Maya at 20:30 UTC. Handoff message when stable.
deploy-bot: Observability note: Traces for failing requests show most failures at envoy->target handshake; retries often succeed on different AZ target.
Luis (support): Customers notified. No major SLA escalations yet. Keeping status page updated with 'partial degradation'.
Erin (on-call): Current status: partial degradation in eu region; mitigation steps in place (conntrack bump, envoy restarts, ALB weight shift). Monitoring for 15m. If errors drop below 3% sustained, we move to status: degraded -> resolved.
Jon (netops): ALB 5xx rate now at 4.1% EU (from 38%). Connection reset rate dropping. Continuing to monitor.
Anna (infra): Provider has scheduled deeper host-level investigation; will update here. We may need to drain and replace 6 instances if hardware issue confirmed.
Maya (eng-sre): Kicking off data capture for RCA. Will create postmortem draft after stability.
Erin (on-call): Handoff now to @Maya for RCA and closure. I’ll remain available for customer escalations. Closing live mitigation loop. :white_check_mark:
Maya (eng-sre): Acknowledged. Recording timeline and next steps. Setting follow-up ping in 2 hours for root cause update.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=high, impact=partial_eu, commander=Erin, assignee=Maya, incident_id=INC-2026-1955554321
